args: set -euo pipefail; t=$(mktemp -d); cargo install -q --path crates/cli --root "$t/bin"; export PATH="$t/bin/bin:$PATH"; awk '/^## Walkthrough/{f=1;next} /^## /{f=0} f' README.md | awk '/^```/{c=!c;next} c' > "$t/walkthrough.sh"; test -s "$t/walkthrough.sh"; cd "$t" && bash -euo pipefail walkthrough.sh; d=$(find "$t" -name decisions.jsonl | head -n 1); test -n "$d"; tail -n 1 "$d" | jq -e '.winner != null'

evidence_required: Output of cargo clippy -p tier-drop-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings.
Walkthrough transcript from a temporary directory ending with a non-null winner.
objective: Implement the tier-drop CLI over the core with an append-only hashed JSONL ledger, integration tests and the README walkthrough.

outputs.purpose: CLI manifest with the tier-drop binary.
Integration tests over the built binary.
Workspace lockfile updated for the CLI dependencies.

risk_controls: Ledger writes are append-only; nothing rewrites an existing line.
Only the README Walkthrough section is written; the rest of README.md is kept.
Rust by default; strict TypeScript only in adapters/dsh; no Python and no authored .js, .mjs or .cjs files.
No secret, phone number, account identifier or internal hostname in any file; run gitleaks protect --staged --redact before each commit.
Never write the owner's private organisation name (search pattern O[K]OA) or the forbidden owner-framing phrase (search pattern needs[ ]you) into any file; plain, specific prose.
Work only in the slice's worktree and branch; never touch main.
steps: clap derive CLI exactly as the "CLI surface" table in plan/technology-decisions.md.
Ledger module: append-only JSONL writes with O_APPEND, canonical JSON lines, record_sha256 filled before write, verify recomputing hashes and reporting file:line, show filtering.

attempt record reads the attempt from stdin, validates it against the task and registry, fills record_sha256, appends, prints the FloorResult, then calls assess_disqualification over the family's attempts for that tier and appends a Disqualification when returned (print it too).
decide loads the ledger's in-force disqualifications and the task's attempts, calls decide, appends and prints.

Integration tests in crates/cli/tests/ using std::process::Command on the built binary (env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_tier-drop")) over a temporary directory: the README walkthrough end to end; ledger tamper detection (T-16); schemas routing_decision title (T-21); exit codes (T-20).

Write the README "Walkthrough" section only (keep the rest): the exact commands a stranger runs (create registry from the example, write a task, plan, record two attempts, decide, verify ledger, export dataset).
